name: documentary
label: Editorial Documentary
description: Real stories told like a streaming documentary: real YouTube footage of the actual events, map animations, real newspaper headlines, real photos and objects, Vox-style collage scenes and quiet, premium graphics. No stock footage, no AI pictures.
tagline: Real stories, told like a streaming documentary.
source_cost_guide: about $0.08 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + collage pictures + cutouts); about $0.50 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: 3d
label: 3D Reconstruction
description: Real stories retold as a premium 3D documentary: the places, the ships, the crowds and the people of the story rebuilt in real-time 3D — faceless white figures in era-correct clothes, real light, fog and weather, drone moves through the scene. Claude directs every shot from the narration, looks at preview stills of each one and fixes what is wrong before the final render on this computer's graphics card. Quiet 2D graphics carry the numbers and dates, maps the routes, real footage the rest.
tagline: History rebuilt in 3D — directed, checked and fixed by Claude before it renders.
source_cost_guide: the voice is about $0.05 a minute; Claude's directing runs on your Claude Code plan (a 10-minute video uses about 5 % of a Claude Max 5x week); the 3D renders on this computer, about 15-20 minutes per minute of video

name: nocturne
label: Dark History 3D
description: True stories of war, spies and assassinations told the way the best 3D history channels tell them: the moments nobody filmed rebuilt in real-time 3D at night — moonlight, haze, silhouettes, FPV drone moves through the clouds and into the scene — cut against short bursts of real black-and-white newsreel on the people and events the narration names. The real photographs lie on a dossier desk under a lamp, a real portrait lights up in a black void, and a negative flash marks every cut between the 3D and the archive. Claude directs every 3D shot from the narration, looks at preview stills of each one and fixes what is wrong before the final render on this computer's graphics card.
tagline: The night nobody filmed, rebuilt in 3D — cut against the real archive.
source_cost_guide: the voice is about $0.05 a minute; the archive film is watched free on the Gemini free tier; Claude's directing runs on your Claude Code plan (a 10-minute video uses about 5 % of a Claude Max 5x week); the 3D renders on this computer, about 10-15 minutes per minute of video

name: quest
label: Level-Up Stories
description: Real history, real careers and real lives played as a bright 3D video game: "Level 1. You're a recruit…". The viewer is the hero — a chibi toy figure with a face, who levels up through every rank in a low-poly toy world while a game HUD tracks it all: the level badge and rank, an XP bar, three stat bars, quests that count up, an item hotbar, level-up cards with a golden sunburst, item pickups, unlocks, a boss bar and achievements. Claude designs the playthrough from the script (the levels, the hero's outfit at every rank, the stats, the quests) and directs every 3D shot; this computer's graphics card renders it.
tagline: Every level of anything — played as a 3D video game, with a full game HUD.
source_cost_guide: the voice is about $0.05 a minute; Claude's game design and directing run on your Claude Code plan (a 10-minute video uses about 5 % of a Claude Max 5x week); the 3D renders on this computer, about 15-20 minutes per minute of video

name: courtside
label: Sports Rise & Fall
description: Sports and NBA documentaries cut like a streaming film: real game footage, real photos of every player named (never AI), old newspapers animated on screen, Kodak contact strips, an old television for archive footage, cinematic black-and-white maps, article lines over darkened photos, stats tables, chapter cards, real interview clips with their own sound, and a VHS grade for the old stories — clean and modern for a young star like Lamine Yamal. The story comes first: cold open, rise, fall, what remains.
tagline: Real photos, old newspapers, Kodak strips, VHS — the story first.
source_cost_guide: about $0.04 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cutouts); about $0.60 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: jung
label: Dark Psychology
description: The original Frontier look and the cheapest way to make long videos: stock footage, AI pictures and motion graphics under a calm narrator. Dark psychology in the tradition of Carl Jung — rewrite it for your own niche.
tagline: The original Frontier look, built for long videos.
source_cost_guide: about $0.05 a minute — about $1–2 for a 30-minute video

name: stories
label: 2D Life Stories
description: Second-person money stories told over years, drawn as flat 2D cartoons with one recurring main character, the same face and clothes in every frame. Replace the cast and the art direction with your own.
tagline: Second-person money stories, told over the years.
source_cost_guide: about $0.15 per minute of video

name: avatar
label: AI Avatar
description: The cheap tier of the presenter channel: a real-looking person opens the video, then photographs drawn for the exact words carry it. No motion graphics, no generated clips, one face. About a tenth of what a produced video costs.
tagline: A face people trust, then the pictures do the talking.
source_cost_guide: about $0.11 a minute

name: avatar-premium
label: AI Avatar Premium
description: The produced tier. The presenter comes back through the whole video — from a different camera each time, beside the picture or in a corner of it — and every claim he makes is restated on screen as one clean object: a number the size of the frame, a rule with its conditions, two things compared. Pictures move where movement earns its place.
tagline: He says it. The screen proves it.
source_cost_guide: about $0.90 a minute

name: modern-homes
label: Home & DIY Tips
description: Practical home advice told by a person on camera, framed in a rounded card over warm paper, with big serif titles that land one line at a time. Products, cleaning, repairs and what is quietly wasting your money.
tagline: Plain home advice from someone who has actually done it.
source_cost_guide: about $0.09 a minute with pictures only, $0.11 with everything on

name: workshop
label: Old-Timer Tips
description: The man who has done the job for forty years shows you how, on paper. He is on screen about 18 seconds of every minute — at the bench, by the fire, out in the yard, a different camera every time — and what he explains is drawn as a hand-tinted engraving on an aged sheet laid over his own place: the cut, the tool, the wrong way beside the right one, the list he keeps. His rules land on torn paper strips over the picture, struck out in red or ticked in green. The video is numbered, and the row of chapters in the corner fills in as he goes.
tagline: Forty years of doing it, drawn on paper.
source_cost_guide: about $0.70 a minute

name: pitmaster
label: BBQ & Cooking Tips
description: An old pitmaster talks to you from beside his smoker, one cook at a time, and the drawings on aged paper show the cut, the fire and the wrong way beside the right one. Every video also sells his own illustrated pit book: halfway through he points at the real lesson number, the pages land on the table, and a card with a QR code and the video's own short link sends the viewer to the book.
tagline: Sixty years on the pit — and his book in every video.
source_cost_guide: about $0.50 a minute

name: mentor
label: AI Mentor
description: A real-looking presenter teaches from a dim modern boardroom, and the graphics live in his shot: glossy glass cards slide past him at table height, a neon countdown hangs in front of him, a glass badge beside his head drains to a percentage, his example prompt types itself into a chat bar. The edit keeps moving — wide, medium, close, slow pushes in and out — and between his shots a 2D cartoon of him acts the story out, with big glass objects and real things turning in the light.
tagline: He teaches it. The screen builds around him.
source_cost_guide: about $2.50 a minute

name: dossier
label: True Crime Case Files
description: True crime and internet mysteries told as a case file on a black table: real footage lying on an aviation chart under a spotlight, real posts and documents as cards, notices and messages typed out like a teletype, a red crosshair on what was found, the main person's name in gold serif, a tracking box on the suspect, two-colour dialogue between police and suspect, and a typewriter caption in the corner. Web pages, real photos, maps in a chart skin.
tagline: A case file on a black table: typed alerts, red crosshairs, real documents.
source_cost_guide: about $0.04 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cutouts); about $0.30 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: kinetic
label: Kinetic Text Essay
description: Essays where the words are the picture: one huge word on a turn, the clip pinned to a chalkboard with the line written under it in chalk, chalk line drawings that draw themselves (a lightbulb, a brain, an arrow, a clock, a target), white line-drawn stills that sketch themselves on, phone cards stacking then scattering round a serif title, a real comment with its phrases highlighted, headlines scrolling by, sources typed with a cursor. Lowercase techno-mono captions at the bottom, the key word yellow.
tagline: The words are the picture: clusters, white pages, phone cards, comments.
source_cost_guide: about $0.10 a minute (voice + four drawn stills + cutouts); YouTube watching is free on the Gemini tier

name: atlas
label: Cartoon History
description: History explained in a thick-outline cartoon world: every picture drawn flat with bold black outlines and a yellowed-paper palette, a TIME MACHINE bar at the bottom when the story jumps in time, a flipchart of eras and dynasties, a wristwatch showing the year, a bouncy title card, paint-wave wipes between chapters, scoreboards of armies and gold, a signpost of where the story could go, cartoon maps with thick outlines and handwritten names, and comic captions. Playful narration, real facts.
tagline: History as a bold cartoon: the time machine, the flipchart, the paint wipe.
source_cost_guide: about $0.15 a minute (voice + twelve drawn stills) plus about $0.50 once for four Seedance clips

name: deep
label: Military & Tech Mysteries
description: Submarines, spy missions, lost aircraft, rockets and the machines behind them, told in teal and orange: real archive footage in a dark monitor with a timecode, stencilled datelines over the picture, an abstract route chart of the journey, a cutaway of the vessel with the crew as glowing figures and the ones the story follows in red, a sonar screen of contacts, a classified readout of the facts, the wall map of a headquarters the camera pushes into, two-tone maps with a white route, and pictures drawn as matte 3D renders where no footage exists. No captions.
tagline: Teal and orange: stencil dates, sonar, cutaways, the map room.
source_cost_guide: about $0.03 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cutouts); about $0.30 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: news
label: Geopolitics Explained
description: Wars, crises and elections explained like a newsroom's best segment: real news footage full frame with a breaking band and a crawling ticker, relief maps with the story's country pale cyan, the neighbours salmon, red heat and yellow dots where it burns, arrows of movement between named places, boxed place labels pinned on the footage, the same public figure in panels across the years, real quotes from real reports as lower thirds, figures counting up with their source, real article pages. No captions; the labels do the talking.
tagline: A newsroom's best segment: heat maps, arrows, tickers, panels over time.
source_cost_guide: about $0.05 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cutouts) plus about $0.15 per presenter appearance; about $0.30 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: legend
label: Legend Reveals
description: "John Daly Reveals the 5 Most Special Golfers He Ever Saw" — told by John Daly. The film opens on a real clip of the athlete or star talking on camera, about twenty seconds; their voice is cloned from that very clip, and the story continues in the first person, in their voice, over real footage and real photos of every person named. They are never shown again. Warm memoir look: photos centred over a blurred copy with a cream keyline, a yellow-bordered close-up inset sliding in, numbered chapter cards for each person on the list, lower thirds, scorecards, the narrator's own line as a card, dated years. No captions.
tagline: A real clip, then the story in the star's own cloned voice.
source_cost_guide: about $0.03 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cutouts; the voice clone is free on the Professional plan); about $0.30 a minute on paid credits

name: hustle
label: Side Hustle Explainer
description: Side hustles, online business and money explainers with the energy of the best young creators: footage on a dark glossy stage with a glow and a drop shadow, big two-to-four-word captions popping in the middle with the key word in red, DIFFICULTY LEVEL bars filling segment by segment, glossy 3D icons with one word, money raining over the footage, corner titles with a glossy blob logo, counters rolling up to the figure, one option versus another on scored bars, checklists ticked one by one. Fast cuts, punchy grade.
tagline: Glossy black, glow, difficulty bars, money rain, counters.
source_cost_guide: about $0.15 a minute (voice + a drawn picture every 7 s + cutouts); YouTube watching is free on the Gemini tier

name: pulse
label: AI News Briefing
description: This week's AI news, edited like a launch film. A presenter opens every video and comes back through it; each update arrives on the company's own official logo, its real benchmark chart, its real launch post and real screen recordings of the thing working. Big hairline type on near-black, one sentence at a time on white when something needs thinking about, numbers that count up, and a chapter counter that tells you which of the twelve updates you are on.
tagline: Twelve updates, twelve chapters: official logos, real benchmarks, real posts, a presenter who comes back.
source_cost_guide: about $0.25 a minute for footage, pages and graphics, plus the ai33 voice, plus about $0.23 per presenter appearance on kie Kling

name: almanac
label: Retro Archive Doc
description: History told like an encyclopedia entry you cannot put down: who someone was, what a thing was, and how one led to the other. Real archive film and real photographs, printed in three inks — mustard, ink black, paper white. Names rise out of dark bars beside each person's real photo, the objects the story turns on become collector's cards, the era's film runs through a 35 mm strip, every frame its own shot, that spins down onto one frame and dives into it, big figures ring up on cash-register drums, and the verdict is proofed on a printing press and stamped.
tagline: The history of people and things, printed like an almanac: real archive film, collector's cards, press proofs.
source_cost_guide: about $0.05 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + cut-outs); about $0.60 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: horizon
label: Charts & Numbers
description: Big questions answered with real numbers: why a country stopped having children, how a currency collapsed, what an ageing world will look like. Real news footage full frame, and between it the numbers drawn big and calm on a near-black navy — the line a country draws while the camera follows its pen, a population pyramid turning over from 1960 to 2100, a hundred people shrinking to five across four generations, a figure that rolls like an odometer, countries side by side, a real document on the table with its translation, a real person's words typed as the narrator reads them. Every figure comes from the World Bank or the UN, fetched by the engine, and the script is fact-checked before the voice. Real newspaper headlines, maps, the real people named, interview soundbites with subtitles. No captions.
tagline: Real numbers, drawn big: charts, pyramids, documents, quotes.
source_cost_guide: about $0.05 a minute with the Gemini free tier (voice + photo cut-outs); the World Bank and UN data is free; about $0.30 a minute when footage is watched on paid credits

name: folio
label: Illustrated Explainer
description: An animated history-and-science explainer that looks like a picture book coming to life. Every frame is an illustration drawn in code: flat shapes with soft gradients, one warm light you can see, depth of field, cartoon people with big eyes who look the same all film, small serif labels for places, years and names, and engineering diagrams on cream paper ('Fig. 1') whenever the story explains how something works. A calm narrator, a soft score, no footage and no captions.
tagline: A moving picture book: every shot drawn in code, every number on screen, every 'how' on paper.
source_cost_guide: the voice costs cents; Claude draws every shot on your Claude Code plan — about $7 of Opus a minute at API prices (a 10-minute video is roughly 2 % of a Claude Max 20x week); rendering runs on this computer, about 20 minutes per minute of video in all

name: hacker
label: Hacker Stories
description: True stories of hackers, hacker groups, cyber attacks and the people who stop them, told as a fast documentary made almost entirely of motion graphics on pure black. Colour is the side: the hackers are green neon line figures, the enemy is red, police, agencies and platforms are blue, neutral facts are white. Every date decodes out of pixel noise, every number rolls up in pixel digits, every place is found on a dark globe that whip-spins to it or a flat dark map that fills it, every person or institution the hackers deal with is a glass badge at the end of a dotted line. Posts, intercepted messages and documents are rebuilt as dark cards and taped paper notes with red stamps and yellow highlighter; a hidden speaker's words are typed beside a line mask in a monitor. Real footage appears only inside a dark monitor turned in 3D that powers on with a glitch. Chapters open on dripping red titles with the music up. No captions.
tagline: Neon hackers on black, colour-coded sides, globes, pixel decodes, rebuilt posts.
source_cost_guide: about $0.05 a minute with the Gemini free tier (the voice); the graphics are drawn on your computer, no image models

name: history
label: Painted History
description: Long-form history told calmly and in order — how a city, an empire or a dynasty rose and changed — in sepia oil paintings that move slowly and dissolve into each other, and an embossed parchment map where empires spread, armies march and battles are marked. Every place, event and dynasty gets a title in Roman capitals, every ruler a round gold-rimmed portrait, the great turning points burn through like paper. No footage, no captions: paintings, maps and a deep, even narrator over an orchestral score.
tagline: History in oil paintings and parchment maps.
source_cost_guide: about $0.10 a minute (the paintings and the voice) plus $1.50–3 a video for up to ten paintings set in motion (Seedance on kie.ai, $0.15 a 5-second clip); no footage to watch; rendering takes about eight to ten minutes per minute of video
